answers.answer: Exactly one handler bypasses compose. The code uses instanceof Promise to select the Promise path. For a direct non-Promise null or undefined, it calls not-found without checking finalized. That fallback lies outside the direct handler catch. Other non-nullish direct values pass through unchanged. In the Promise path, a truthy resolved value wins. A falsy resolved value uses c.res if finalized; otherwise it calls not-found. Rejections in that chain go to the private error handler. In composition, each handler result is awaited. A falsy result skips response assignment. If no handler is selected, not-found runs only when finalized is exactly false and the callback exists. After the runner completes, the application dispatcher requires a finalized context. If it is unfinalized, it raises an Error within its composed-path catch scope; otherwise it returns context.res.

answers.answer: In the composed frame, a truthy result is assigned only when the context is not finalized or the result came through onError. A normal returned response therefore cannot replace a finalized response through this condition. A truthy onError result can. A falsy result skips this assignment. Direct use of the res setter can replace stored response state and sets finalized to true, including for undefined, if the setter reaches those final assignments. Header merging occurs first and can fail before that update. When old and new responses both exist, the setter copies the new response and merges old headers except old content-type; old set-cookie values replace the new cookie collection. Merely reading res can create response storage without finalizing it.

answers.answer: Each runner starts its progression index at -1. A child dispatch with i less than or equal to the last dispatched index rejects with the repeated-next Error. This guard executes before that child frame enters its handler try/catch. It therefore bypasses its own handler catch. If an awaiting parent handler receives that rejection, the parent frame can handle the Error through onError when that callback exists. A propagated Error can also reach the application dispatcher. The code does not guarantee that a user handler awaits next, so an unawaited continuation is not guaranteed to reach the parent catch. A non-Error value or an Error without onError is rethrown by that frame.

answers.answer: The response-state concept links response storage and finalized across the functions. finalized starts false. The res getter can create storage and prepared headers without setting finalized. The res setter writes storage and sets finalized true if its earlier work succeeds. The direct-next callback awaits not-found and assigns through that setter. The Promise-result callback reads finalized to choose between stored response and fallback. The nested middleware dispatcher reads this state to decide whether to call not-found or assign a result. The composed-finalization wrapper checks it after the runner and returns context.res or raises an Error. The application dispatcher connects those paths. These records do not prove that all possible application writes are represented.
